utterances.text: We had stopped at Defence Exhibit 300, which is actually an order --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Nobilo, for barging in. When I'm saying, Mr. Nobilo, that the accused is testifying, I want this to appear on the transcript. I want the public to know that Mr. Blaskic is the accused present in this trial and is testifying. What I mean is that the accused in this case is testifying, and I would like this little nuance to appear on the transcript. Our hearings are public, and it is useful for the public to know exactly at what stage of the trial we find ourselves, a trial which, let me remind you, started some 20 months ago. All right. Let us continue. Thank you to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We had stopped before the lunch break when we were discussing Defence Exhibit 300, which is the order for combat operation which you issued to the Ban Josip Jelacic Brigade in Kiseljak on the 17th of April, 1993 at 21.45. We were starting to analyse and discuss Zavrtaljka, which is a key strategic point in that part of Kiseljak. Let me ask you in relation to point 2 where you say -- in 2.2, you say, among other things, that mortars should be used to systematically target and capture this point. Could you please explain to the Court what, in your military terminology, the words "systematic fire" means?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In this point, 2.2, it says, "By systematic targeting, by mortar launches of 60, 82, and 122-millimetres capture Gomionica and Svinjarevo." "Systematic fire" implies the greatest possible precision when using mortars, especially when the targets are military, that is, the deployment or position of forces that are being attacked, the firing positions of individual artillery pieces which are the object of attack, but with the greatest possible precision and accuracy.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What would be the opposite term? If you were not to use this term, "systematic," how do you describe it then?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Then the order would say, "Carry out firing of the targets with 60, 82, and 120-millimetre mortars," and in practice, that would mean opening fire at the whole position where the enemy unit is positioned without the requirement of the greatest possible precision in respect to each individual point. Such a targeting of the object would be carried out in a far shorter period of time and with far less precision.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In this same point, you instruct the units, in continuation of the operation, to attack and capture Bilalovac. What was the reason for your instructions to direct them towards Bilalovac, and what did Bilalovac mean then?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Bilalovac was the first point where the main communication between Kiseljak and Busovaca, the main road, had been intercepted. At that time, any attack or offensive operation towards Bilalovac would mean the stretching out of forces for Busovaca and Vitez, the stretching out of the front line, because the command of the 3rd Corps would resolutely defend that corridor which links Zenica via Fojnica with Konjic and Mostar. Therefore, my basic idea was to alleviate the pressure on Vitez and Busovaca by forcing the 3rd Corps to deploy a part of the forces at the Kiseljak front.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please remind us in what area the BH army, in January '93, captured the road between Kiseljak and Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can show that to you. The Kacuni-Bilalovac segment of the road was captured. This was a land and air corridor enabling operational linkage of the 3rd Corps of the BH army with the 6th and 4th Corps of the BH army in Fojnica and Konjic or, rather, Konjic and Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: If, by some good fortune for your units, you had managed to make a breakthrough from Bilalovac towards Busovaca, what would that mean for your operational position in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That would certainly have radically changed the impossible situation we were in in Vitez, and it would give us greater hope that we would be able to hold on to these areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let me summarise: Attacks in the direction of the villages of Gomionica, Svinjarevo, and Bilalovac, was their aim exclusively a military one or was it not?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: My view is that it was exclusively a military objective, and that was the only way for me to improve the situation in Vitez and Busovaca, which were virtually on the brink of falling.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: To alleviate the situation in Vitez and Busovaca, what did you have to attack? Who did you have to attack?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I had to give an order for an attack against the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina so that the main forces of the BH army would regroup and focus on the Kiseljak theatre of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us go on to point 3. You say that Fojnica, according to your order, must secure your left flank and launch an attack on Dusina or a breakthrough towards Sebesic. What does that sentence mean in military terms?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the event that the Ban Josip Jelacic Brigade from Kiseljak were to start an attack towards Bilalovac, then the entire left flank would be vulnerable and that would enable a part of the forces of the Visoko Operative Group of the BH army to launch an attack somewhere and to inflict losses on the left flank. That is why I issued the order that Fojnica must secure the left flank, and it was alternatively, either that it should attack the Dusina detachment of the BH army, which was deployed in the region of the village of Dusina, or to take action in the direction of Sebesic and to deblock the Sebesic HVO, which was totally surrounded by BH army forces already at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us in summary form, what was the aim of engaging HVO units from Fojnica? Was the aim to aggravate relations between Croats and Muslims in Fojnica or was there some other reason?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The only reason was to alleviate the position of the forces attacking from Fojnica to the south of Busovaca by linking the main forces of the BH army and to ease the pressure on the southern part of the Busovaca theatre of war, Prosje, Polom, Kapak, Busovacke Staje.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In point 5 of your order you say, "To the commander of the Ban Josip Jelacic Brigade," and I quote, "Your estimates about certain forces are basically unfounded and unrealistic because the main forces are concentrated on Vitez and Busovaca." Could you please explain to the Court the meaning behind this sentence?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: According to the information available to us, the main forces of the 3rd Corps, to which the forces of the 1st Corps of the BH army had been attached, and which were organised into an operative group called Visoko, they were engaging in an offensive operation against Busovaca and Vitez, and auxiliary forces of the BH army were, ever since the January conflict, January '93, on the point of contact between the Kiseljak line -- this is the Kiseljak theatre war and the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you remind us where this line was?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That front line was from Zavrtaljka via Pobrdze, Velike Sotnice, Hrastovi, Male Sotnice, Barane, Gunjace, Kazagici, Grabovi, Hadrovci, Svinjarevo, Gomionica, Sikulja, Podastinjsko Brdo or hill, and Tusnjici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The commander of the Ban Josip Jelacic Brigade, did he share your view that the main forces were at Kiseljak and Busovaca, and the auxiliary ones in Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In his report, his view was that the main forces were concentrated at the Fojnica theatre war, that is in the zone of responsibility of the Ban Josip Jelacic Brigade, and that is why I told him that his assessments were not correct because I had information, and I was aware of the impossible situation in Vitez and Busovaca, and that is why I told him that the main forces were not on the Kiseljak front line, but on the front line of Busovaca and Vitez, that is, the main forces of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: To make it quite clear, did you believe that there were no BH army forces in Gomionica, Svinjarevo, and the part of the front which you have just described?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I looked upon this situation from the standpoint of the concentration of the overall forces of the 3rd Corps, and my position was that the main forces under the command of the 3rd Corps command were engaged in the attack on Busovaca and Vitez, whereas the auxiliary forces of the 3rd Corps, which were also quite strong but not as strong as the main forces were at the Kiseljak front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In your next point or one of the next points, that is point 7, it says, "All army forces, police forces (military and civilian) are to be placed under the command of the Ban Josip Jelacic Brigade in Kiseljak." Tell the Court, on the basis of what authority are you giving this order for the military and civilian police to be attached to the Ban Josip Jelacic Brigade?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the basis of the authority given to me by the main staff in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Point 8 says, "All assault operations must be successful, and to that end, use units of the military and civilian police for the mop-up." Could you explain what this mop-up, mopping up operations for a solder in this kind of operation, meant?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When a unit is carrying out an attack and the front line is broken through, the front line of the defender, what happens usually is the stage of retreat by the defence forces, and for the attacker, the stage of pursuit, and efforts to maintain combat contact. For the other pockets and strongholds of fire, these are usually neutralised by mopping-up forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How would you define the mopping up of the area? What does that mean for a soldier?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: For a soldier, that meant neutralisation of remaining pockets of fire, then of crew members left behind in bunkers or in firing positions, that is, the remainder of forces that are still resisting. Otherwise, mopping up is a tactical operation, which is regulated in the rules of the infantry, and in the rules of the companies, and platoons on which the basis of training is carried out in infantry units, from the level of a squad, through a platoon, and a company. The subject taught is usually a company in attack, a platoon in attack, and one of the subjects discussed or one of the issues that soldiers are trained for, are mopping-up operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us assume that HVO units make a breakthrough, and push back units of the BH army, and pursue them deep in the territory under BH army control. Where do these pockets of resistance remain in relation to the HVO?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the rear of HVO units, behind the backs of those units.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let me ask you quite openly. This military term from training sessions called "mopping up," does it have anything to do with ethnic cleansing, or the concept of expulsion of civilians?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honours, this can be checked in all the rules and regulations of the former JNA. There is absolutely nothing in common, and the infantry rules describe in detail the task of mopping-up groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: One further point. You are writing to the Ban Josip Jelacic Brigade the following: "Maintain a sense of historic responsibility." What did you really mean? What did you use such strong words in this order?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was fully aware of the seriousness of the whole situation, and I knew that survival, especially in Vitez, depended exclusively on the actions of the Ban Josip Jelacic Brigade. If they had not carried out this assignment, further to this order, it is highly probably that on the 18th, in the morning, the area of Vitez would have been captured by the BH army forces because we had started talks on a cease-fire, and we didn't manage to come to an agreement and implement them. Then we also tried using people of authority to mediate and affect a cessation of hostilities. That failed too. We tried to alleviate the situation with false attacks from the direction of Zepce. This did not reduce the intensity of attack either, and for some time in Vitez, we were logistically completely cut off from logistic bases of the main staff, which were located in Herzegovina, in the course of the fighting on the 16th, also from the logistic base in Stojkovici, so that we had a major shortage of ammunition, and there was no way out. The situation was, in fact, on the brink of collapse.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This Defence Exhibit, this order, was given to the Defence by the Office of the Prosecutor. Therefore, clearly, this is the form in which the order was drafted, and the form in which it was received in Fojnica, an area which was later captured by the BH army, but tell the Court how this order was seen, how it was dispatched. Was it by packet radio? If not, why not?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I assume that it was sent by telefax and not by packet, by radio.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Because, you mean, a stamp and a signature cannot be sent by packet radio?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. This order is signed and stamped, but not only on those grounds am I saying this. Our aim was primarily to ease the pressure on the Busovaca-Vitez front line, and I assume, I cannot be sure, but I assume that the command of the 3rd Corps also has this order because in Kacuni it could easily get a copy of this order from the telefax.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So you sent this by civilian telefax, using a civilian line?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, the most ordinary telefax line, from Vitez to Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Were you aware, at the time, that the BH army would be able to read it and recognise it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I knew that the mail in Kacuni was operational, the post office in Kacuni was operational, because it had been the subject of a discussion in February '93 already, between representatives of the joint commission of the HVO and the BH army, but my main purpose was to hold on to our territory and ease the pressure on the Vitez-Busovaca front. Even if they do get hold of this order, they will react sooner and withdraw their forces from this front.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can we say that it was, in fact, in your interest that they learn about it as soon as possible?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us proceed. Document D297, please. This document that you issued on the 17th of April, 1993, at 20.00, to the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade, and to the commander of the Vitez Brigade, for his information, it has to do with reinforcements for the Vitez forces, and you're ordering that 25 to 30 men from the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade in Novi Travnik come to Vitez, and place themselves at the disposal of the Vitez Brigade, and under their command, in order to help in the defence of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Were 25 to 30 men sufficient in such a critical situation as you described? Why didn't you ask for 300 men to come to your assistance, armed and with ammunition?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Twenty-five to 30 men were not sufficient. We needed much more, more than 300, in fact, but I had been in touch with the commander of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade, and I also realised that the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade was holding the entire front line facing the Republika Srpska army in Novi Travnik, and that together with the Travnik HVO units, it held 80 kilometres of the front with the Serb army, and this was the maximum number of men that they could afford to give me, so that they may be placed under the command of the commander of the Vitez Brigade to assist in defending the village of Krcevine where the line had been broken through, and where the danger threatened of forces being linked with those in Stari Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Why didn't you order the whole brigade to abandon the front with the Serbs, and to transfer to the front with the new aggressor? Wouldn't that brigade have been very welcome to you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I personally did not believe that the situation was so critical that the BH army was the new aggressor, and my priority was still, at the time, defence against the army of Republika Srpska. HVO units did not abandon a single position that they held in '92, on the front line, toward the army of Republika Srpska in Novi Travnik, and also in Travnik, on the basis of any orders. The priority was to defend against the possible attack of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This order talks about attachment or resubordination. We discussed yesterday the question of the unit that was attached to you, and you said it is the moment when a unit is reporting to the person it is being attached to, and this was at 11.42 in that situation. Tell us, in this document, in this order, where can we see the moment when the commander of the Vitez Brigade becomes the commander of these 25 to 30 men? Please read the order and explain it to us.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is point 2, and I am reading it, "In the execution of this order, make contact with the commander of the Viteska Brigade, whose duty it is to organise introduction into combat of your unit."

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The question is: From what moment on does the commander of the Viteska Brigade command these men from Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: From the moment when the commander of the Novi Travnik unit reaches Vitez and reports to the commander of the Vitez Brigade, saying that he was reporting, together with his unit, and putting himself and his unit at his disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is this stated in point 2, with the words, "Make contact with the commander of the Viteska Brigade"?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next document, please, D298. So document 298 was also written on the 17th of April, 1993, at 20.00 hours. You are issuing an order to your brigades, and also independent units such as the Vitezovi and the military police, and you are ordering maximum combat readiness. Among other things, you are abolishing all possibility of leave, furlough, and you say everybody must take part in the defence, et cetera, et cetera. Question number one: On the second day of the war, at 20.00 hours, practically in the evening, why are you ordering maximum combat readiness of the units? Isn't that action that was supposed to take place before the outbreak of the conflict? Isn't this a kind of action that is supposed to be done beforehand, rather than two days after the conflict breaks out?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Certainly. Raising the level of combat readiness is sometimes done beforehand. However, the situation on the ground obviously showed that not all were yet aware that this was an all-out attack by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and that its ultimate objective was to take the Lasva Valley, and break the HVO in Vitez and in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In the preamble of this order, you are mentioning the order of the HVO main staff, and then the number is written by hand, dated the 17th of April, 1993. Do you perhaps recall which order this was?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It does have a hand-written number here, but I presume that this order is actually simply an implementation of the order issued by the main staff. I cannot say that for sure, but it does say, "On the basis of the HVO main staff commander," and then the number is mentioned, "02-2/1-01-64," and I'm not even sure whether this is a zero, of the 17th of April, 1993, "The aggression of Muslim forces against the HVO forces and the Croatian people, I hereby order..." I believe that all these points are also contained in the order of the main staff commander as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In point 3, you say, "All available potentials in the zone of responsibility should be used for defence purposes, and force to be used if necessary." What does this actually mean?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That means that all men, weapons, and military equipment should be used for defence purposes in the zone of responsibility of those units to whom this order pertains.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When you say "force," what does "force" mean in the context of this order?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It means military conscripts of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You mean those who would refuse to go to the front?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And now, please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Break. We could take a break. A 15-minute break maybe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The hearing is resumed. Mr. Nobilo, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Document D288, did you receive that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have 298.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: D288, D289, D291, D292, D293, D294, and D295, so all of those documents, please. Very briefly, D288 and the other reports too. Very briefly, though, D288, is that the report that you got from the Busovaca Brigade on the 17th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Document D289, is that the document that you got on the 17th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This document was sent on the 17th of April, 1993, but it says that it was received on the 16th of April, 1993 at 8.35. That's what the stamp at the bottom says.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So what is your conclusion? What happened?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Probably there was a mistake with the date of reception because it seems that it was received before it was sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But now you can see it; right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The next one, 291, this is from Zenica. It is entitled "Request."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, please, the document which appears on the screen, which appears on the ELMO, which document is it? According to the registry, it's document D291.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That's right. That's right. Yes, that is document 291 that we're going to be speaking about. It is precisely that document, the 17th of April, 1993, at 10.20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It's number D291 which is on the screen; am I right? The one starting with the words "HVO members in the Stranjani village"; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Then we all agree. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell me, General, this is a report from the HVO of Zenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The handwriting on this report, is this your handwriting maybe?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Take a look at one thing. It was written on the 17th of April, 1993 at 10.20, and it seems, according to the stamp, that it was received at 10.32 on the 18th of April, 1993, that is to say, with a one-day delay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can we have this put on the ELMO, this document, please? Now we can see it, the original stamp. Could we have it blown up a bit, please, this stamp, so that we can see when it arrived in Vitez? Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: It's the 18th of April, 1993 at 10.32. It travelled for an entire day. What's all this about?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that time, there was obstruction on the packet radio, and I think that there were other such cases too that these packet communications were not functioning or at least not functioning from time to time or with major delays.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Court, technically, how does one obstruct packet communication? I know that it is not your line of work, but very briefly.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, it would be sufficient to have one radio transmitter and an antenna and to work previously on the same frequency of 146 megahertz, and in this way, the receiver could not receive the incoming messages, and, of course, the situation was even more difficult during combat operations and when the entire area from Zenica to Vitez was flooded with various messages and radio communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please remind us, these packet communications, they went via computer and radio, that is to say, through airwaves, radio waves?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. In addition to that, you needed a modem, a computer modem, and a radio station, and these radio waves were used to send messages.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us have a look at the next document, D292. This is a report from the Busovaca Brigade of Nikola Subic-Zrinjski sent to you on the 17th of April, 1993 at 12.00, and the stamp of reception shows that you received it only on the 27th of April at 13.40.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I would like to have this stamp shown on the ELMO, please, and I would like it to be enlarged as much as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That is to say, there is a 10-day difference. How do you explain that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, there were the same problems, obstruction of the packet communications, and also there was interception, et cetera, by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: However, realistically speaking, the elements of this report and of the previous report from Zenica and this one from Busovaca, did you, nevertheless, receive these facts on the day of the 17th of April, 1993 when you found out about this?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I had telephone communication with the commanders on an open telephone line so that I did receive information and facts from the commanders in direct communication with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: If you were to rely exclusively on packet communication, and if you didn't have any telephones or if the telephone lines went through enemy territory and you knew that it would be intercepted through Kacuni towards Kiseljak, would packet communications, as such, be sufficient for you? Would you have enough information to be able to command?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us go on to the next document, D293. This is a report from the Vitez Brigade. We won't read it. Just tell us whether you received it on the 17th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next document, D295. D295 is also a report of the Busovaca Brigade dated the 17th of April, 1993. Did you receive it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Document 295, in my hands, is a report from the Vitez Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. It's a report from the Vitez Brigade. The number is 295. Did you receive it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Apart from these reports and the reports that you received orally and which you mentioned in the operations diary in your testimony yesterday and today, did you learn anything else on the 17th of April that would lead you to believe that anyone was intentionally destroying civilian facilities or killing civilians?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you now tell us in a couple of sentences, on the 17th of April, was that day, for you, a day of military success or failure?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That day, for the Operative Zone and the HVO, was, in military terms, unsuccessful and certainly one of the worst days from the standpoint of the military situation because we were totally encircled in Vitez, and all tactical positions north of the road, the Vitez-Travnik road, had been captured by the BH army. Also in the territory of Zenica municipality, the Croatian villages in the region of Gornja Zenica or Upper Zenica were surrounded, and the civilian population had started to move out towards the Travnik municipality under pressure of the forces of the BH army. From the village of Cukle in Travnik municipality, one half of the villagers left the village in fear and under pressure of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the situation in Busovaca municipality was such that we lost all the territory of Jelinak, Bakir, and a part of Prosje in Kacuni, and we found ourselves totally encircled. From the military standpoint north of Vitez, not a single tactical position was under the control of the HVO from the 17th of April, 1993, which would give us a chance to carry out our defence successfully.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us go on to the events of the 18th of April, 1993, the day when there were fewer events, but, in any event, this is the last day that we will deal with in such a chronological manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The 18th.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, the 18th.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 18th of April at 00.20, I spoke to the main staff of the HVO, the main headquarters, and I informed them about the situation in Zenica according to the reports I had received from the Zenica HVO commander. I said that there were murders, arrests, persecution, looting, torching which were being committed against HVO members and the Croats of Zenica by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. At 00.50, I talked to the deputy commander of the Zenica HVO Brigade and informed him that I had managed to pass on all information and to brief the main staff of the HVO in Mostar on the situation and the position of the HVO in Zenica. From the deputy commander of the Zenica HVO, I requested that he try to prevent panic within HVO ranks. At 00.51, a report reached us from the Military Intelligence Service that the positions of the BH army in Rovna and Pezici had had the following casualties: One dead member of the Muslim armed forces and three wounded, and that the troops of the Muslim armed forces who were on these positions were exhausted. At 00.55, I called the United Nations command and asked to speak to Colonel Stewart. I was not able to talk to him, but I did talk to the officer on duty from the UN Battalion, and I asked him for assistance for the Croatian villages of Upper Zenica, which were surrounded by BH army forces. At 06.00, the commander or the deputy commander, rather, of the Zenica HVO Brigade called up and informed me that at 05.30 an attack had been carried out against the HVO brigade command in Zenica by the forces of the 3rd Corps of the BH army and from three directions and that the HVO command in Zenica was encircled. He also told me, I mean the commander of the Zenica HVO, Vinko Baresic, that he would have to abandon the command and pull out to the following position: In the direction of Cajdras. At 06.10, I issued an order, number 01-4-337/93, dated 18, April, 1993, and the content of the order was destruction of documents of the command of the Zenica Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What was the reason for you to take such a measure?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The command of the HVO brigade in Zenica, due to the assault by the BH army, had to abandon its command post, and they didn't have enough time to take with them the documents, and the documents they could not carry, I ordered them to be destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is this a routine military measure in the event of evacuation?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is always done when we were not able to move, in a planned manner and organised manner, the command from one position to another. At 06.22, I received a report from Zenica that all communication with the command of the Vitez Operative Zone had to be suspended, and that they were moving from the former command post, in the direction of Cajdras. They told me they would call once the moving had been completed. At 06.24, I spoke to the artillery commander, and asked that they prepare for fire against target 1, and to economise with the ammunition. At 06.31, I received a report from the Travnik Brigade, number 06-267/93, dated 18 April, '93, at 06.00 is the time it was sent, and the content of the report was that in the night, that is of the 17th of April, at about 22.00, the village of Cukle had been abandoned, and that half the population moved out, and UNPROFOR was informed of this. The village had been abandoned by the Croats. The UNPROFOR was probably also informed about it by the Travnik Brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you remember the reason for the Croats to flee their village of Cukle?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is a village on the fringes of the Travnik municipality, and the reason was the pressure of the BH army forces because the Travnik-Ovnak-Zenica road had already been blocked by the BH army forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At 06.54, the commander, Vinko Baresic, from Zenica, called up by phone and asked for urgent assistance from UNPROFOR, complaining that the situation was very grave, and that they virtually had no way out. I told Vinko that I would immediately call UNPROFOR, and ask them to block the approaches to the Croat villages, so as to protect the Croats in Zenica. I also asked him to try and organise himself in order to gain time. At 07.05, I again called the main headquarters in Mostar, and conveyed to them the report I had received from Zenica about the very difficult situation there, and I informed the main staff that I had tried to get in touch with UNPROFOR, but that I had still not managed to do so, that is, to have the UN go to Zenica, and I told them that we needed food, and ammunition. I also told them that in Zenica there were about 100 dead, and I asked them to let me know when Brigadier Petkovic, the chief of staff, arrives in the main headquarters, so that I could inform him in person.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When you said a hundred casualties, what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I mean dead. At 07.06, I was called out by the commander of the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade, and I gave him instructions and explanations on the basis of the written order that I had formerly issued. At 07.12, I again called the UN command, but nobody answered my call. At 07.15, I called Vlado Juric, from the air defence battalion, and asked him to send a light launcher to the Vitez Brigade. At 07.35, I was informed that the command of the Zenica Brigade had moved to the building of the command of the 1st HVO Brigade Battalion from Zenica. An order had also been issued, number 01-4-343/93, dated 18 April, 1993, at 07.30 hours, and I think it had to do with the designation of personnel to replace members of the military police on the front line. The order was addressed to the Vitez Brigade. At 07.55, I got in touch with the UNPROFOR command in Nova Bila, and I informed them that we needed assistance, and the touring of the villages of upper Zenica. The villages were Podbrezje, Broda, Cajdras, and Janjac, in which the Croat inhabitants had been surrounded by members of the BH army. At 08.50 (sic), I was called by the commander of the 1st Battalion in Zenica, who informed me that a large number of civilians was arriving in the village of Cajdras, and that many of them were gathering around the church, and that among them there were some soldiers belonging to the HVO in Zenica. I gave him instructions that they should organise themselves, and protect themselves from shelling, and that for our part, we would do everything in our power to assist them, as far as we were able. I told him that we had already asked for UN members to block the roads and to protect the civilian population. At 08.10, I spoke again with the UNPROFOR command, asking them to protect the Croats of Zenica from BH army attacks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: 08.10. Previously there was a mistake. We see in the transcript "08.50," but it should be "08.05" in the previous paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At 08.05, I spoke to the commander of the 1st Battalion, and at 8.10, I spoke to the UN command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: 08.05, five minutes past eight. That's been corrected now, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At 08.10, I spoke to an officer from UNPROFOR, asking again for protection for the Croats in the villages of upper Zenica, and his answer was that UNPROFOR forces were unable to provide assistance straightaway because it overstepped their mandate, until a representative of the International Red Cross does not arrive and join in, but the UN promised me that they would visit the villages, as I had asked, that is, the village of Perin Han, Podbrezje, Broda, Cajdras, Janjac, and Raspotocje, and that they would convey to us what they learned about the situation in those villages. At 08.25, I was informed, by Mayor Santic, of the plan to pull out Muslims with the help of UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What did that mean?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was a report that UNPROFOR forces were probably participating in the evacuation of Bosniak Muslims from certain areas of Vitez municipality, or of wounded, or endangered Bosniak Muslims, or dead Bosniak Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Apart from this information conveyed to you by the mayor, therefore, a civilian official, were you, in any sense, a participant in the organisation of this evacuation? When I say "you," I mean the HVO under your command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Just a second. You were informed. What was your reaction? I did not understand what you said. You are informed of this? You are informed that there is an evacuation planned for Bosniak Muslims. How do you react? What do you do?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I only received information about a plan to have UNPROFOR get the Bosniak Muslims out, Mr. President. I did not receive information as to the localities involved. It was probably the area of Vitez. Which particular area, I did not know at the time. I don't know now, until this present day, what position was actually involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So apart from what is written down here, you do not have any other information? You don't remember anything else?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, nothing except for this at 08.25.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you know whether action was taken according to this plan or not, or do you know anything else?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know, today, on the basis of the witnesses that were heard here, that there was evacuation, with the assistance of UNPROFOR, of Bosniak Muslims from the village of Veceriska, but I don't know whether this plan, about which I only received information in this form, pertained precisely to that village and to that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At 08.28, I received information from the head of the Military Intelligence Service that a message had been intercepted or, rather, recorded, of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which reads as follows, I quote: "Convey Cajdras has been broken. HVO forces are moving towards you. Prepare a welcome for them."

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This quotation is a message that was intercepted, and this was actually communication between two units of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At 08.35, I was called by Mario Cerkez, Commander Mario Cerkez, who informed me that there were frequent calls from Croats in Zenica. They were seeking help and reporting on the difficult situation there. At 08.45, I received a call from Commander Siljeg, from the Operative Zone of North-western Herzegovina, and I informed him about the situation in Zenica being critical, that during the course of the morning, the command of the HVO brigade in Zenica was attacked, and that it was expelled, and I told him that he should convey to the chief of main staff that the situation in my area, that is to say, the Vitez area, was critical too. At 10.30, I asked the commander of the artillery to prepare for fire at targets trig 603, trig 591, and target 594, 500 metres to the south. At 10.00, that is to say, 52 minutes past 10.00 (sic), I talked to Fra Bozo, the parish priest from Cajdras, who informed me that many civilians had gathered around the church in Cajdras, and that they were afraid. I told Bozo that they should protect themselves from the shelling, and that we called the UN At 10.58, I had a conversation with UNPROFOR, and I asked whether they had visited Croat villages in the municipality of Zenica that I asked them to visit, and I had asked that at 08.10. I was informed from UNPROFOR that teams were on their way to these villages, and that I should call back within an hour or two. At 11.40, Commander Cerkez informed me that the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was carrying out intensive operations from the positions of Sljibcica. At 11.52, the head of the Military Intelligence Service provided me with information to the effect that in the village of Kajmakovici, the area of Vranjska, there were mortars of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina that were firing. At 12.00, we checked with the Vitez Brigade the order to have a replacement carried out for 40 soldiers. At 12.02, we received information on intensive operations that were carried out by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, from the positions of Sivrino Selo. At 12.04, we received information from the communications centre that there was packet communication every now and then. At 12.06, information was sent about the situation in the zone of responsibility for the command of the 101st XP Brigade in Zenica, number 01-4-353/93, dated the 18th of April, '93. At 12.15, a worker from the prison in Zenica informed us that the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was bringing in larger numbers of Croats to the penitentiary in Zenica, that is to say, to the gaol in Zenica. At 12.18, a statement was released to the public, to all the media of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, number 08-4-351/93. At 12.25, Mario Cerkez called, the commander of the Vitez Brigade, and he provided information to the following: That the replacements for the mentioned 40 soldiers were not ready yet, but that work on this was under way. At 12.35, I received a call from Mr. Dario Kordic, who conveyed a piece of information to me from Mr. Mate Boban, that we should hold out, and that they were working and trying to help the negotiations. At 12.38, I called the artillery commander, and I sought information on the situation regarding ammunition for the artillery. He asked for one hour in order to be able to provide information on this. At 12.50, I had a conversation with Mr. Franjo Boras, who called --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you please tell us which post Mr. Boras held then?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was a member of the war presidency of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and a member of the supreme command of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I told him the following: I am checking the situation there where there are no crazy people from our side.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is that a literal translation of what you told him then?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. "Here," and I'm referring to Zenica, "is where the situation is the worst. According to reports we've been receiving for there, they are slaughtering people in Zenica."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Just a minute. I haven't understood you well. I think maybe there was a slight interpretation mistake. Maybe we will have a break shortly. You talk about the head of staff of Bosnia-Herzegovina. You tell that man, "I control the situation," and after that, I haven't understood what you've said. Could you please go over what you said to Mr. Boras, and I think that will also help the interpreter who had a hard time understanding you. After that, we will have a short break. What did you tell Mr. Boras, please?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, Mr. Boras was not a member of the main staff. He was a member of the supreme command of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well then. What did you say to him?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I told him the following: "I have under my control the situation there where there are no crazy people. Here, in Zenica, it is the worst. In Crkvica, they are slaughtering, according to the reports that are coming in --"

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please, let us stop at this point. Who is slaughtering who? When you are saying that they are slaughtering, who is slaughtering who?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The members of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina are slaughtering HVO soldiers and Croat civilians, according to the reports that I had been receiving. I told Mr. Boras too, according to reports that were coming into us, that is what I said specifically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine. Maybe you are a bit tired, Mr. Blaskic. I think the interpreters may be tired as well. We will take a 15-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The hearing is resumed. Mr. Nobilo, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We stopped after the conversation you had at 12.50 with Franjo Boras, member of the presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and then the Presiding Judge, the Honourable Judge Jorda, asked you what you exactly told him. Could you please tell us what you talked about to him and what you told him exactly?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I informed Mr. Franjo Boras that I did have under my control the situation there where there were no madmen, that in Zenica, the situation was the worst, particularly in Crkvica, according to the reports that they were coming in, that they were slaughtering, that the church in Podbrezje was torched, looted, damaged, and that within the compound of the Zenica steelworks, there were BH army members, that they were getting out of there, and that UNPROFOR and the European Monitoring Mission did not see this, that I didn't know anything about Commander Totic from Zenica and the four officers of the command of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade from Novi Travnik, that two officers, members of the command of the Operative Zone, had been wounded as they were returning from negotiations held at the UNPROFOR base and that they were wounded by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and that combat operations were still under way, intensive combat operations at that, that I sent three requests to the 3rd Corps concerning Zivko and the four officers, but for the time being, that I did not have any response. "Yesterday, UNPROFOR did not transport the wounded HVO soldiers from the medical centre to the church hospital," and that we were trying, through the European Monitoring Mission too, to pacify the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please, could you just explain one thing: What did you mean when you said, "I have under my control the situation there where there are no madmen." Where did you have the situation under your control, and where were there madmen?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: According to the reports and information I had received, the situation was chaotic and out of control in the area of Zenica, and, literally, I was receiving information to the following effect: "They are crazy; they are slaughtering," and they were actually referring to the Mujahedeen from the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And control? Where did you manage to protect the population? Territorially speaking, where was this?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, mainly Vitez and Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please proceed with this chronology. After this conversation was over, what happened in the Operative Zone?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At 13.15, a press release was released, number 08-4-351/93. At 13.23, I asked the commander of the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade to send me more frequent reports and more complete reports about the situation. At 13.50, I asked the artillery commander to fire at the Samar target. At 14.05, we instructed the IPD assistants. This was number 08-4-352/93. At 14.08, I informed Commander Kraljevic as follows: "You are getting support. Follow this and observe." At 14.16, I talked to the MTD commander, that is to say, the artillery commander, and I was checking whether he was actually firing as requested. He told me, "Yes," and he asked me to inform him about observation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In the case of Commander Kraljevic and in this report of the artillery commander, when you're talking about observation, what does that actually mean?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, the artillery commander had his own observation positions from which he could see whether the targets were hit and whether there should be any correction. We also asked that every commander who seeks support from artillery should have his own observers and that he should inform us about where the target was actually hit. So the artillery commander always received two pieces of information about a single shot. One piece of information was from his own observers, that is to say, from the artillery observers, and the other piece of information was from the observers of that unit that support was being given to. So we corrected this, and we also checked whether the targets had been hit as we compared both sets of data.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At 14.18, I received information from the commander of the Vitez Brigade that Donja Veceriska was completely abandoned. There were neither soldiers there belonging to the BH army nor any inhabitants, Bosniak Muslims, in that village.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Later on, what did you learn? In what way did the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the inhabitants leave Donja Veceriska and with whose assistance?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I learnt later on that UNPROFOR came, upon the request of the commander of the BH army in Donja Veceriska, to evacuate the wounded but that when the UNPROFOR vehicle set off with the wounded, it was followed by the entire population of Donja Veceriska, together with UNPROFOR, in the direction of the UN base.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The military units of Donja Veceriska, where did they go?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They retreated gradually, first to Divjak and then towards Grbavica, and they spent some length of time at Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please continue with the chronology.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At 14.21, I called the commander from Zepce, the commander of the 111th Special Purpose Brigade. The officer on duty reported, and I asked them to remain in position for future assignments, and those assignments had to do with the staging of a false attack from Zepce towards Zenica. At 14.28, I was informed by the artillery that the target had been fired at as instructed. At 14.34, I called the commander of the civilian police in Vitez, Mr. Samija, and asked him, if possible, could his intervention platoon of the civilian police be sent as a reinforcement to the commander of the Vitez Brigade, underlining that the matter was urgent. At 14.35, the artillery commander called in connection with the report on the situation regarding ammunition, and the artillery commander said that, by packet communication of the head of the Military Intelligence Service, this report on ammunition would be sent to us. At 14.50, I talked to the officer on duty of the 4th Battalion of the military police, and I learned from him that the civilian police was on the line facing Mahala and that the security of the hotel or, rather, the command of the Operative Zone would remain as for the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mahala is also the region called Stari Vitez; is that so?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. At 14.55, I tasked Slavko Marin to draft a request for the supply of a telefax from the military police. At 15.00, I received a report from the head of the Military Intelligence Service in which he reported that the BH army was preparing an ambush for HVO forces in the area between the village of Jardol and Grbavica, which is the area of the Varupa houses. At 15.05, Slavko Marin called the command of the Vitez Brigade and conveyed to them this information and the warning regarding the ambush being prepared by the BH army. At 15.07, I spoke to the artillery commander and asked him to fire at target 810, and the commander informed me that, for the moment, they were unable to hit that target.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell the Court, we see that you often communicate with the artillery commander. Where was he based? Was he based where the artillery pieces were stationed, and how was it organised?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He had his base in Nova Bila, and the artillery pieces were positioned at firing positions. Then also there is the commander of the firing position who received orders from the artillery commander for the opening of fire and supervised work at the firing position, and the artillery commander spent most of his time in his command post at Nova Bila.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At 15.12, I checked again with the artillery commander to see whether he was preparing for target 810. At 15.25, I asked him to fire at target 810. At 15.34, I was visited by a captain from the UN, I think his name was Captain Matthew, and he asked to visit Rovna. I told him that he should wait for awhile so that we could inform the forces that were in contact so that they could provide security for his safe passage to Rovna.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who held Rovna? Under whose control was it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: A part of Rovna was in the hands of the BH army and a second part in the hands of the HVO, but the border between the two was between the municipality of Busovaca and Vitez, so it was rather complicated to provide complete security. The front line was virtually passing through the middle of that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I asked Captain Matthew whether UNPROFOR had visited Cajdras and whether he had any information about the Croatian villages of Zenica, and he told me that Colonel Stewart himself had gone to Zenica but that, for the moment, he was not aware of the exact whereabouts of Colonel Stewart nor the information available to Colonel Stewart himself. At 15.43, I spoke again with the artillery commander and inquired about the execution of fire, and he told me that he was still having difficulties. At 15.48, the artillery commander called me and informed me that there was a problem with the second artillery piece.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What do you mean by this problem?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It means that there were certain technical difficulties and that the crew manning the artillery piece was unable to carry out fire as requested, and, if possible, every effort was made to remove the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At 15.59, I called the artillery commander again and asked him to check who was or, rather, which crew was currently manning the artillery pieces. At 16.07, Slavko Marin called the commander of the Travnik Brigade and checked with him the information received that Travnik was absolutely blocked for any traffic. The commander of the Travnik Brigade confirmed this report, that Travnik was blocked, that is, all the roads were blocked, and that negotiations were under way between representatives of the HVO and the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and that once any agreements were reached, they would inform us. Travnik, at the time, was blocked by checkpoints held by BH army units. At 16.09, I required that the artillery commander fire at target 915 with one projectile, when he was ready to do so. At 16.12, I received a message from the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade, number 783/'93, dated 18 April, '93 at 14.00. The report contained data regarding the number of dead. This report said that 9 soldiers had been killed, and 21 soldiers wounded. I don't remember the rest of the contents of that report. At 16.20, I had a report from the head of the Military Intelligence Service, to the effect that the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was preparing to open fire on the position Apoteka, or the pharmacy, in the town of Vitez, and that it was necessary to remove from that position both personnel and artillery. This is an information that we conveyed to the Vitez Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said "artillery," and you used the word "artillery piece." Did you mean anything else?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I cannot say with precision what was next to the pharmacy. Whether it was an infantry or an artillery weapon, I don't know. At 16.22, Slavko Marin called the commander of the 111th Special Purpose Brigade in Zepce, Mr. Ivo Lozancic, and asked him to be ready at 18.00, for movement as ordered. Again, this was part of the staging of a false attack. At 16.38, I was called by Brigadier Petkovic, the chief of staff of the main staff of the HVO, who informed me that a truce had come into effect with the BH army, and he ordered me to call Enver, and to check whether Enver had received any order from Sefer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us, please, Enver was the commander of the 3rd Corps, and Sefer was the chief of staff of the main staff of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I informed Brigadier Petkovic that I was having serious problems in Zenica, that I too wanted to receive that order in person, the order on the cessation of fire that he had referred to, and I said that I would call the commander of the 3rd Corps, and immediately inform him, orally, about the order for a cease-fire. At 16.40, I was called by Vinko Baresic, the deputy commander from Zenica, who informed me about the very difficult situation there, and I told him that an agreement on a truce had been signed, and that we were awaiting an order on a cease-fire, and that we were suspending combat operations, but if the BH army continues its attacks, we would have to defend ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: General, let's stop just a moment to combine the orders with your own statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can I have D316, and D318, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So Exhibit D316 is the order of the chief of staff of the HVO, Brigadier Mile Petkovic, issued to your Operative Zone, and to another three Operative Zones where HVO units were stationed. The heading is, "Cessation of Hostilities Between the BH Army and the HVO. Order. On the basis of the conclusions reached after the talks between Mr. Mate Boban and Mr. Alija Izetbegovic, which took place on the 18th of April, 1993, in Zagreb, and in accordance with point 3 of the agreement, I hereby order: 1. All HVO units shall immediately cease hostilities with BH army units. 2. The exchange of prisoners, both soldiers and civilians, shall start immediately. 3. The wounded shall be cared for, regardless of which forces they belong to. 4. Reliable information shall be gathered concerning the protagonists of the conflict, the expulsion of the civilian population, the killing of captured soldiers and civilians, the torching of houses and other buildings. 5. Contact shall be established with the BH army command, asking them to implement the same order. 6. All HVO units shall be familiarised with this order immediately." As I said, it is addressed to Central Bosnia, the Operative Zone of Northwest Herzegovina, the Operative Zone of Southeast Herzegovina. During the talks, or after the talks, did you receive this order in writing, by packet communications?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: After the conversation, I received the order from the chief of staff, Brigadier Petkovic, and I said, a moment ago, that already at 16.40, I informed Vinko Baresic, the HVO commander in Zenica, about the order on cessation of hostilities, but at that moment, I did not convey all the points to him because I didn't have the document in my hands at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us go on to document D308. It is your order, in English, 01-4-363/93, and it is addressed to the commanders of all HVO units in the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia; to the BritBat commander, Colonel Stewart; the European Monitoring Mission; and the 3rd Corps of the BH army in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Will you look at that order, please? Did you write that, and sign this order, and send it to the addressees indicated in the heading?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did sign it. I wrote the order in Croatian. I gave it to Ms. Vanja Saric to translate it. She translated it into English. I signed the order. I called Colonel Stewart, or the officer on duty in the UNPROFOR command in Nova Bila, and I asked them to mediate in conveying this order to the 3rd Corps commander in Zenica, because we'll say later on in the chronology, I was told, in the 3rd Corps, that they had not received the order on a cessation of hostilities. So in order that the UNPROFOR should not waste time translating the order, I sent it immediately in English to the UNPROFOR command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: As far as you can remember, is it correct that all the six points from the order of Brigadier Petkovic, regarding cessation of fire, exchange of prisoners, investigating the protagonists of the expulsions, and killings, and torchings, et cetera, that you literally copied all six points, and included them in this order and dispatched them to various units?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that is true because the order of my commander was based on an agreement which I didn't have a copy of, so I based my order on the order of the commander of the main staff. So literally, whatever is contained in the first order, is contained in the order that I wrote.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Fine. Let us go back to the chronology of events in the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia. You ended your conversation with Brigadier Petkovic, and then with Baresic from the Zenica brigade, at 16.40. What happened next?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At 16.48, I was called by the duty officer from the main staff of the HVO, and he asked to hear about the situation briefly. I told him that I had already submitted a report, and that we had many casualties. I also said that from here, meaning Vitez, they could not expel us because we had no place to go, and that they can only make another Vukovar out of us, but that we had no place to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you please explain to the Court what kind of a symbol Vukovar is with Croats? Why did you say, "You can make another Vukovar out of us"? What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that moment, what I told the duty officer of the main staff is that the army could not drive us out of Vitez. He sort of laughed because he said, "Yes, you have no place to go to." Vukovar was a symbol of suffering at that time, the greatest suffering in Croatia, and that was my association, that now we were in a situation of total encirclement, total siege, and without any possibilities to get out of that encirclement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is it true that the town of Vukovar, the Eastern Slovenia-Croatian town of Vukovar, was fully under siege, and that it was totally destroyed as it was being taken?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At 16.55, I sent an order to the 4th Battalion of the military police, number 01-4-359/93, dated 18th of April, '93 at 16.30. The content of the order is as follows: That members of the military police should be replaced at the front line. At 17.00, again I had a conversation with the main staff of the HVO at Mostar, and I provided them with information that there were still problems in Zenica, and that attacks coming from Zenica were the strongest, that I received an order, and that I informed them about the cease-fire, that the town of Travnik was blocked, and that currently there were negotiations under way in Travnik between the commander of the Travnik Brigade, and the commander of the forces of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and that in Novi Travnik, there was high tension. I also said that many people were afflicted, and at 17.20, I had the impression that the hotel had been hit, and, at that time, we thought that was a shell, a mortar shell from a 120-millimetre mortar, because the entire building of the hotel shook, and we thought that the hotel itself was directly hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Court what entry was made then in the operative log, that you think that it was hit, or that it was hit?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Literally, it said that the hotel was hit by a 120-millimetre shell, from the direction of Preocica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What does Preocica mean? What did you mean by saying "Preocica"?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was the position of the forces of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that was Preocica, on the right hand of Preocica, actually, between two hills, where there was artillery and/or tanks all the time. Sometimes it was a tank, and sometimes it was artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At 17.27, the Military Intelligence Service --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You mean the Military Intelligence Service?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: -- yes, the Military Intelligence Service, that the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was firing with artillery at Kovacevac, 500 metres to the south. At 17.30, the head of communications from the main staff of the HVO of Mostar called, and he asked who held the post office, the PPT communications, in Travnik. We informed him that communications were under the control of the members of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. At 17.30, an answer was sent to the Zenica Brigade, number 01-4-354/93, dated 18th of April, 1993, and it was related to a document that we had received from Zenica, number 6383/93, dated 18th of April, '93, at 10.32. I assume that this was information in writing about the situation in Zenica, but do I not recall the contents. At 17.40, I talked to a member of the command in Fojnica, and I asked for a report on the situation in Fojnica. At 17.50, I received information from the head of the Military Intelligence Service, that the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina would soon operate in the area around the church in Stari Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is that a Catholic church?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it is a Catholic church. Information was intercepted on orders to open artillery fire towards the Catholic church, towards the area of the Catholic church, because that is literally what it says here, it says the "area." So it wasn't actually the church that was a target. At 17.55, I received information that Jure Krezic, Commander Jure Krezic, was killed. At 18.26, I received information from the head of the communications centre that the packet communications with Zenica were dead once again. At 18.40, I received information from the commander of the Vitez Brigade about the situation, and the officer of this district, Mr. Vid Jazbinski, established contact with the commander of the 3rd Corps, and he checked whether they received orders on cease-fire, that is, the order that we looked at a few minutes ago. The reply of the officer from the 3rd Corps was that they did not receive orders to cease fire. I personally talked to the representative of the 3rd Corps then. I'm not sure whether it was the commander of the 3rd Corps or, that is to say, Mr. Enver Hadzihasanovic, or the duty officer of the 3rd Corps, but I read all the points of the order that I had received from the main staff regarding the cease-fire, and I said, "Well, we are going to send you now, via UNPROFOR, a copy of the order that we had issued to our units." At 19.30, I was informed, by Vinko Baresic from the Zenica Brigade, that he was compelled to sign a surrender of the HVO in Cajdras, in Zenica. At 20.40, Slavko Marin talked to the commander of the Vitez Brigade in connection with the organisation of the defence, according to sectors, and the way in which smaller roads would be built in order to link Vitez with the hospital. At 21.00 hours, I had a meeting with Commander Cerkez, with the head of the defence department in Vitez, and the mayor of Vitez, in connection with the organisation of defence according to sectors, and also the building of smaller roads for wartime purposes, in order to link Vitez to Busovaca and the hospital. At 22.00, I sent an oral report to the main staff of the HVO, on the momentary situation in Central Bosnia. At 23.00, I talked to Brigadier Petkovic, and I informed him that the situation was quite critical and serious, and that I was asking for help from a top political level, in order to carry out the signed cease-fire, that is to say, the signed agreement and the order on cease-fire. At 01.40, on the 19th of April, I received information on regrouping and concentrating strong forces of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the area to the north of Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, in this way we have completed the chronology for the 18th of April, and it is 5.30. It's past 5.30 now, so perhaps we could finish for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. We won't go any further today. We'll meet tomorrow at 2.00 -- no, sorry, 1.30. As tomorrow is Wednesday, we'll meet at 1.30 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
